The last 5 questions are a data-interpretation set based on one table; the set stays together.

questions.sub_topic: Ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
questions.question: Who is the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
options: B) The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) The Vice-President of India
Why: Under Article 64, the Vice-President is the ex officio Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).
Why not the others: (B) presides over the Lok Sabha. (C) is part of Parliament but presides over neither House. (D) is a member of one House and leads the government.
Key point: The Rajya Sabha also elects a Deputy Chairman from among its members.

questions.sub_topic: Third tallest of five boys
questions.question: Among five boys, A is taller than B but shorter than C. D is shorter than B. E is taller than C. Who is the third tallest?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) A
Answer steps: from the clues, E > C > A > B > D. The third tallest is A.
Why not the others: (A) C is second. (C) B is fourth. (D) D is the shortest.
Key point: Build one line from tallest to shortest before answering.

questions.sub_topic: Difference between two shares in a ratio
questions.question: ₹1,800 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. How much more does C get than A?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) ₹400
Given: ratio 2 : 3 : 4, total ₹1,800.
Step 1: One part = 1800 ÷ (2 + 3 + 4) = ₹200.
Step 2: C = 4 × 200 = ₹800; A = 2 × 200 = ₹400.
Step 3: Difference = ₹400.
Common mistake: giving one part (₹200, option A), or giving C's whole share (₹800, option B).

questions.sub_topic: Author of The Discovery of India
questions.question: Who wrote "The Discovery of India"?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Jawaharlal Nehru
Why: Jawaharlal Nehru wrote "The Discovery of India" in 1944 while imprisoned in Ahmednagar Fort.
Why not the others: (B) wrote "Hind Swaraj" and "The Story of My Experiments with Truth". (C) wrote "Gitanjali". (D) wrote "India Wins Freedom".
Key point: Nehru also wrote "Glimpses of World History" (letters to his daughter Indira).

questions.sub_topic: Statements about the Paris Agreement
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Paris Agreement on climate change:
A. It was adopted at COP21 in 2015.
B. It aims to keep the rise in global average temperature well below 2 °C above pre-industrial levels, and to try to limit it to 1.5 °C.
C. Under it, countries submit Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs).
D. It sets binding emission-cut targets only for developed countries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A, B and C only
C) B, C and D only
D) A, B, C and D
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) A, B and C only
Why: A, B and C are correct: the agreement was adopted in Paris in December 2015, sets the "well below 2 °C" goal, and asks every country to set its own targets (NDCs) and update them every five years.
Why not the others: D is wrong: binding targets only for developed countries were a feature of the Kyoto Protocol (1997); under Paris, all countries make pledges. Options (C) and (D) include D; (B) leaves out the correct statement C.
Key point: Kyoto — targets for developed countries only; Paris — pledges by all.

questions.sub_topic: Two trains passing in opposite directions
questions.question: Two trains, 120 m and 180 m long, run on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 50 km/h and 40 km/h. How long do they take to pass each other completely?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 12 seconds
Given: lengths 120 m and 180 m; speeds 50 and 40 km/h in opposite directions.
Step 1: Relative speed = 50 + 40 = 90 km/h = 90 × 5/18 = 25 m/s.
Step 2: Distance = 120 + 180 = 300 m.
Step 3: Time = 300 ÷ 25 = 12 seconds.
Common mistake: subtracting the speeds as if the trains ran the same way (10 km/h, giving 108 seconds, option A), or using only the longer train's length (180 ÷ 25 = 7.2 seconds, option D).

questions.sub_topic: Spacecraft that brought Sunita Williams home
questions.question: On 18 March 2025, astronauts Sunita Williams and Butch Wilmore returned to Earth after about nine months in space. Which spacecraft brought them back?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) SpaceX Crew Dragon
Why: They had flown to the ISS on Boeing's Starliner in June 2024 for a short test flight, but problems with its thrusters meant it returned empty. They came home with the Crew-9 team aboard a SpaceX Dragon, splashing down off Florida.
Why not the others: (A) was the craft they went up in. (C) is a Russian craft. (D) is NASA's capsule for the Artemis Moon missions.
Key point: Their stay was about 286 days instead of the planned eight.

questions.sub_topic: Total students taking two languages
questions.question: In a class, every student takes Hindi or Sanskrit or both. 25 students take Hindi, 30 take Sanskrit and 12 take both. How many students are there in the class?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 43
Answer steps: total = 25 + 30 − 12 = 43.
Why not the others: (A) adds the two groups without removing the overlap. (C) subtracts the overlap twice. (D) adds the overlap instead of removing it.
Key point: n(A or B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(both).

questions.sub_topic: Colour of light with the longest wavelength
questions.question: Which colour of visible light has the longest wavelength?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Red
Why: In the visible spectrum, red light has the longest wavelength (about 700 nm) and violet the shortest (about 400 nm).
Why not the others: (A) has the shortest wavelength. (B) and (C) lie in between.
Key point: Red light scatters least, which is why danger signals are red.

questions.sub_topic: Winner of the World Test Championship final 2025
questions.question: Which team won the ICC World Test Championship final at Lord's in June 2025?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) South Africa
Why: South Africa, led by Temba Bavuma, beat Australia by five wickets, chasing 282 with Aiden Markram scoring 136. It was South Africa's first ICC title since 1998.
Why not the others: (A) lost the final. (D) won the first final in 2021. (B) lost the first two finals (2021 and 2023).
Key point: WTC winners — New Zealand 2021, Australia 2023, South Africa 2025.

questions.sub_topic: Height of a tower from the angle of elevation
questions.question: From a point on the ground 30 m from the foot of a tower, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is 60°. What is the height of the tower?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 30√3 m
Given: horizontal distance 30 m; angle of elevation 60°.
Step 1: tan 60° = height ÷ 30, and tan 60° = √3.
Step 2: Height = 30√3 m (about 52 m).
Common mistake: using tan 30° = 1/√3 (10√3 m, option A), or using cos 60° = 1/2 (15 m, option D).

questions.sub_topic: Founder of the Arya Samaj
questions.question: Who founded the Arya Samaj in 1875?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Dayananda Saraswati
Why: Swami Dayananda Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in Bombay in 1875. He called for a return to the Vedas ("Go back to the Vedas") and wrote "Satyarth Prakash".
Why not the others: (A) founded the Brahmo Samaj (1828). (B) founded the Ramakrishna Mission (1897). (C) founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (1873).
Key point: Brahmo Samaj 1828; Satyashodhak Samaj 1873; Arya Samaj 1875; Ramakrishna Mission 1897.

questions.sub_topic: Five people on the floors of a building
questions.question: Five people P, Q, R, S and T live on the five floors of a building, one on each floor (floor 1 is the lowest, floor 5 the top). S lives on the top floor. P lives on an even-numbered floor. T lives below P but not on floor 1. Q lives on the floor immediately above R. Who lives on floor 2?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Q
Answer steps: S is on floor 5. If P were on floor 2, T would have to be on floor 1, which is not allowed, so P is on floor 4. T is on floor 2 or 3. If T were on floor 2, Q and R would be on floors 1 and 3, which are not next to each other. So T is on floor 3, R on floor 1 and Q on floor 2.
Why not the others: (A) T is on floor 3. (B) R is on floor 1. (D) P is on floor 4.
Key point: Try each possibility for the most limited person and discard the one that breaks a rule.

questions.sub_topic: Code for a word from shared phrases
questions.question: In a certain code, "sky is blue" is written as "pa ri to", "blue sea" as "to mu", and "sky high" as "pa ke". What is the code for "is"?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) ri
Answer steps: "blue" is in the first two phrases, and the code common to them is "to". "sky" is in the first and third phrases, and the code common to them is "pa". So in "sky is blue" = "pa ri to", the remaining word "is" = "ri".
Why not the others: (A) is "sky". (C) is "blue". (D) is "sea".
Key point: Compare phrases two at a time to find the common word and code.

questions.sub_topic: Constant term when roots differ by one
questions.question: The roots of the equation x² − 7x + k = 0 differ by 1. What is the value of k?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 12
Given: let the roots be a and a + 1.
Step 1: Sum of roots = 7, so 2a + 1 = 7 and a = 3; the roots are 3 and 4.
Step 2: Product of roots = k = 3 × 4 = 12.
Common mistake: taking the roots as 5 and 2 (sum 7, product 10, option A), which differ by 3, not 1.

questions.sub_topic: Syllogism of cats, dogs and pets
questions.question:
Statements:
No cat is a dog.
All dogs are pets.
Conclusions:
I. Some pets are not cats.
II. No pet is a cat.
Which of the conclusions follow?
options: C) Both I and II follow
D) Neither I nor II follows
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Only I follows
Answer steps: All dogs are pets, so some pets are dogs; and no dog is a cat, so those pets are not cats — I follows. Cats may still be pets outside the dog circle, so II is not certain.
Why not the others: (B) and (C) accept II, which goes beyond the statements. (D) rejects I, which is certain.
Key point: "All B are C" + "No A is B" gives "Some C are not A".

questions.sub_topic: Assumptions behind a tree-planting decision
questions.question:
Statement: "The government has decided to plant one lakh trees along the highways during this monsoon."
Assumptions:
I. Saplings planted during the monsoon are likely to survive.
II. There is enough space along the highways to plant the trees.
Which of the assumptions is implicit?
options: C) Both I and II are implicit
D) Neither I nor II is implicit
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Both I and II are implicit
Answer steps: Choosing the monsoon for planting takes for granted that saplings do well then (I). Deciding to plant along the highways takes for granted that there is room there (II). Both are assumed.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) each leave out one assumption the decision depends on. (D) rejects both.
Key point: Ask what must be true for the decision to make sense.

questions.sub_topic: Scientists and their discoveries
questions.question:
Match the scientists in List-I with their discoveries in List-II:

List-I
(A) Alexander Fleming
(B) Robert Hooke
(C) Edward Jenner
(D) Gregor Mendel

List-II
(I) Laws of inheritance
(II) Vaccine against smallpox
(III) Penicillin
(IV) The cell
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 (III); Hooke observed and named cells in cork in 1665 (IV); Jenner developed the smallpox vaccine in 1796 (II); Mendel worked out the laws of inheritance from pea plants (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Fleming and Hooke; (B) swaps Hooke and Jenner; (C) swaps Jenner and Mendel.
Key point: Mendel is called the father of genetics.

questions.sub_topic: Writer chosen for the 59th Jnanpith Award
questions.question: The 59th Jnanpith Award, announced in March 2025, was given to which Hindi writer from Chhattisgarh?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Vinod Kumar Shukla
Why: Vinod Kumar Shukla, poet and novelist ("Naukar Ki Kameez", "Deewar Mein Ek Khirkee Rahati Thi"), was named on 22 March 2025. He was the first writer from Chhattisgarh and the 12th Hindi writer to receive India's highest literary award.
Why not the others: (A) shared the 58th award. (B) (Konkani) received the 57th and (C) (Assamese) the 56th.
Key point: The Jnanpith Award is given by the Bharatiya Jnanpith for Indian literature.

questions.sub_topic: Blood vessels that carry blood away from the heart
questions.question: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart to the organs of the body?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Arteries
Why: Arteries carry blood away from the heart under high pressure, so they have thick, elastic walls.
Why not the others: (A) bring blood back to the heart. (C) are the thin vessels where exchange takes place between blood and cells. (D) carry lymph, not blood.
Key point: The pulmonary artery is the one artery that carries deoxygenated blood (to the lungs).

questions.sub_topic: Order of plant groups in primary succession
questions.question:
On bare rock, plant life develops in stages (primary succession). Arrange the following in the order in which they usually appear:
A. Shrubs
B. Lichens
C. Trees
D. Mosses
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) B, D, A, C
Why: Lichens are the pioneers: they break down rock to form a thin soil. Mosses follow, then herbs and shrubs, and finally trees, forming a climax forest.
Why not the others: (A) puts shrubs before mosses. (B) starts with mosses. (D) puts trees before shrubs.
Key point: Lichens are called pioneer species.

questions.sub_topic: Series of squares of primes
questions.question: Which number should come next: 4, 9, 25, 49, 121, … ?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 169
Answer steps: the terms are the squares of the prime numbers — 2², 3², 5², 7², 11² — so the next is 13² = 169.
Why not the others: (A) is 12², (B) is 14² and (C) is 15²; 12, 14 and 15 are not prime.
Key point: Look for squares, cubes or primes hidden in a series.

questions.sub_topic: Odd one out among shapes
questions.question: Choose the one that does not belong with the others: Triangle, Square, Cube, Pentagon
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Cube
Answer steps: a triangle, a square and a pentagon are flat (two-dimensional) shapes. A cube is a solid (three-dimensional) shape.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are all polygons.
Key point: Find the feature that three items share and the fourth lacks.

questions.sub_topic: Profit when buying 12 and selling 10 for the same price
questions.question: A trader buys 12 pens for ₹100 and sells 10 pens for ₹100. What is his profit percentage?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 20%
Given: cost of 12 pens = selling price of 10 pens = ₹100.
Step 1: Take 60 pens (the LCM of 12 and 10). Cost = 5 × 100 = ₹500; selling price = 6 × 100 = ₹600.
Step 2: Profit = 100 on 500, so 20%.
Common mistake: dividing the gain of 2 pens by 12 (16.67%, option B), or taking the difference in the number of pens as the percentage (2%, option C).

questions.sub_topic: Statements about the rivers of peninsular India
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the rivers of peninsular India:
A. The Godavari is the longest river of peninsular India.
B. The Narmada flows eastward into the Bay of Bengal.
C. The Kaveri rises at Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri hills of Karnataka.
D. The Mahanadi flows into the Bay of Bengal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B) A, B and D only
C) A, C and D only
D) B, C and D only
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) A, C and D only
Why: A is correct: the Godavari (about 1,465 km) is the longest peninsular river and is called the "Dakshin Ganga". C is correct. D is correct: the Mahanadi enters the Bay of Bengal in Odisha.
Why not the others: B is wrong: the Narmada (with the Tapi) flows westward through a rift valley into the Arabian Sea. Options (B) and (D) include B; (A) leaves out the correct statement D.
Key point: Narmada and Tapi flow west; most other peninsular rivers flow east.

questions.sub_topic: Constitutional Amendments and their subjects
questions.question:
Match the Constitutional Amendments in List-I with their subjects in List-II:

List-I
(A) 61st Amendment, 1988
(B) 73rd Amendment, 1992
(C) 86th Amendment, 2002
(D) 101st Amendment, 2016

List-II
(I) Goods and Services Tax
(II) Right to education for children aged 6–14
(III) Panchayati Raj institutions
(IV) Voting age lowered from 21 to 18
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: 61st — voting age 18 (IV); 73rd — Panchayati Raj, Part IX (III); 86th — free and compulsory education, Article 21A (II); 101st — GST (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps the 61st and 73rd; (B) swaps the 86th and 101st; (C) swaps the 73rd and 86th.
Key point: The 74th Amendment (1992) did for urban local bodies what the 73rd did for panchayats.

questions.sub_topic: Financial institutions and their roles
questions.question:
Match the institutions in List-I with their main roles in List-II:

List-I
(A) National Statistics Office (NSO)
(B) Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
(C) NABARD
(D) Reserve Bank of India

List-II
(I) Issues currency notes (other than the one-rupee note)
(II) Refinances agricultural and rural credit
(III) Releases official GDP estimates
(IV) Regulates the stock and securities markets
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NSO, under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, releases GDP estimates (III); SEBI (1992 Act) regulates securities markets (IV); NABARD (1982) is the apex bank for agriculture and rural development (II); the RBI issues currency notes, while the one-rupee note is issued by the Ministry of Finance (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps NSO and SEBI; (B) swaps SEBI and NABARD; (D) swaps NABARD and the RBI.
Key point: The RBI was set up in 1935 and nationalised in 1949.

questions.sub_topic: Assertion and reason on sums of primes
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The sum of any two prime numbers is always even.
Reason (R): Every prime number other than 2 is odd.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
Answer steps: (R) is true: any even number above 2 has 2 as a factor, so it is not prime. Because of that, (A) is false: 2 + 3 = 5 and 2 + 7 = 9 are odd. The sum is even only when both primes are odd.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) treat a false Assertion as true.
Key point: One counter-example is enough to show that an "always" statement is false.

questions.sub_topic: Form of carbon that conducts electricity
questions.question: Which form of carbon is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Graphite
Why: In graphite each carbon atom bonds with three others in flat layers, leaving one free electron per atom that can carry current. It is used in electrodes.
Why not the others: (B) bonds every electron, so it does not conduct. (C) and (D) are impure, mostly non-crystalline forms that are poor conductors.
Key point: Diamond — hardest, non-conductor; graphite — soft, conductor.

questions.sub_topic: Number divisible by nine
questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 9?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 5679
Given: a number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 9.
Step 1: Digit sums — 4738: 22; 5679: 27; 3214: 10; 8102: 11.
Step 2: Only 27 is a multiple of 9, so 5679 is divisible by 9 (5679 = 9 × 631).
Common mistake: checking only the last digit, which is the test for 2, 5 or 10, not for 9.

questions.sub_topic: Statements about BRICS in 2025 and 2026
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about BRICS:
A. The 17th BRICS summit was held in Rio de Janeiro in July 2025.
B. India holds the chair of BRICS in 2026.
C. Brazil hosted a BRICS summit for the first time in 2025.
D. Indonesia became a full member of BRICS in January 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A, B and C only
C) B, C and D only
D) A, B and D only
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) A, B and D only
Why: A is correct: the summit met in Rio on 6–7 July 2025 and adopted the Rio de Janeiro Declaration. B is correct: India took over the chair for 2026 and hosts the 18th summit. D is correct: Indonesia joined as a full member in January 2025.
Why not the others: C is wrong: Brazil had hosted BRICS summits before (2010, 2014 and 2019). Options (A) and (C) include C; (B) leaves out the correct statement D.
Key point: India's theme for 2026 expands BRICS as "Building Resilience and Innovation for Cooperation and Sustainability".

questions.sub_topic: Time when clock hands coincide after four
questions.question: At what time between 4 o'clock and 5 o'clock will the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock be together?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 4:21 9/11
Answer steps: at 4:00 the minute hand is 20 minute-spaces behind the hour hand. It gains 55 minute-spaces every 60 minutes, so it needs 20 × 60/55 = 240/11 = 21 9/11 minutes. The hands are together at 4:21 9/11.
Why not the others: (A) forgets that the hour hand also moves. (B) and (C) come from using the wrong rate of gain.
Key point: The minute hand gains 5.5° (or 55/60 of a minute-space) every minute.

questions.sub_topic: Rail project of the Chenab Bridge
questions.question: The Chenab Rail Bridge in Jammu and Kashmir, opened by the Prime Minister on 6 June 2025 as the world's highest railway arch bridge, is part of which project?
options: C) The Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) The Udhampur–Srinagar–Baramulla Rail Link (USBRL)
Why: The bridge, in Reasi district, stands about 359 m above the riverbed, higher than the Eiffel Tower. With the USBRL complete, the Prime Minister also flagged off Vande Bharat trains between Katra and Srinagar, linking the Kashmir valley to the national rail network.
Why not the others: (B) runs along the western coast from Maharashtra to Karnataka. (C) is a goods line from Punjab to West Bengal. (D) is India's first bullet-train line, still under construction.
Key point: India's first cable-stayed rail bridge, at Anji Khad, is on the same line.

questions.sub_topic: Time for the faster of two workers
questions.question: A is twice as efficient as B. Working together, they finish a job in 14 days. How many days would A alone take?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 21 days
Given: if B does x of the work a day, A does 2x.
Step 1: Together 3x = 1/14, so x = 1/42.
Step 2: A's rate = 2/42 = 1/21, so A alone takes 21 days.
Common mistake: giving B's time (42 days, option A), or halving 14 (7 days, option D).

questions.sub_topic: Order of four Mughal emperors
questions.question:
Arrange the following Mughal emperors in the order in which they ruled (earliest first):
A. Shah Jahan
B. Akbar
C. Aurangzeb
D. Jahangir
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) B, D, A, C
Why: Akbar (1556–1605), Jahangir (1605–1627), Shah Jahan (1628–1658) and Aurangzeb (1658–1707).
Why not the others: (A) puts Shah Jahan before Jahangir. (C) puts Jahangir before Akbar. (D) puts Aurangzeb before Shah Jahan.
Key point: Babur, Humayun, Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan, Aurangzeb — "the great six" Mughals.

questions.sub_topic: Cubes cut from a cuboid
questions.question: How many cubes of edge 3 cm can be cut from a cuboid measuring 12 cm × 9 cm × 6 cm?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 24
Given: cuboid 12 × 9 × 6; cube edge 3 cm.
Step 1: Along each edge: 12 ÷ 3 = 4, 9 ÷ 3 = 3, 6 ÷ 3 = 2.
Step 2: Number of cubes = 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 (check: 648 cm³ ÷ 27 cm³ = 24).
Common mistake: dividing the volume by the area of a face of the cube (648 ÷ 9 = 72, option C).

questions.sub_topic: Amount at compound interest for three years
questions.question: What will ₹15,625 amount to in 3 years at 4% per annum, compounded annually?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) ₹17,576
Given: P = ₹15,625, R = 4%, T = 3 years.
Step 1: Amount = 15625 × (1.04)³ = 15625 × (26/25)³.
Step 2: 15625 ÷ 25³ = 1, so amount = 26³ = ₹17,576.
Common mistake: using simple interest (15625 + 3 × 625 = ₹17,500, option A), or working out only one year (₹16,250, option B).

questions.sub_topic: Expression with letters for operations
questions.question: The letters P, Q, R and S stand for '÷', '×', '+' and '−' respectively. Find the value of 36 P 6 Q 3 R 8 S 5.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 21
Answer steps: the expression is 36 ÷ 6 × 3 + 8 − 5. Working left to right for ÷ and ×: 36 ÷ 6 = 6; 6 × 3 = 18. Then 18 + 8 − 5 = 21.
Why not the others: (B) multiplies before dividing (36 ÷ 18 = 2; 2 + 8 − 5 = 5). (C) reads S as '+'. (D) leaves out the + 8.
Key point: Division and multiplication have equal priority and are worked from left to right.

questions.sub_topic: Distance and direction after two walks
questions.question: Town Q is 4 km north of town P. Town R is 3 km east of town Q. How far is R from P, and in which direction?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 5 km north-east
Answer steps: R is 4 km north and 3 km east of P. Distance = √(4² + 3²) = √25 = 5 km, and the direction is north-east.
Why not the others: (A) adds the distances. (B) gives the wrong direction (east, not west). (D) subtracts them.
Key point: Two walks at right angles form the sides of a right triangle.

questions.sub_topic: Relation through grandfather's only son
questions.question: Pointing to a photograph of a girl, Arjun says, "She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son." How is the girl related to Arjun?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Sister
Answer steps: Arjun's grandfather's only son must be Arjun's father. The daughter of Arjun's father is Arjun's sister.
Why not the others: (B) would need the grandfather to have another son or a daughter. (C) is a generation too high. (D) would need Arjun to be the grandfather's only son.
Key point: "Grandfather's only son" (on the father's side) is the speaker's father.

questions.sub_topic: Effect of current used in a fuse
questions.question: An electric fuse protects a circuit by melting when too much current flows. Which effect of electric current does it use?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Heating effect
Why: A fuse wire has a low melting point. When the current is too large, the heat produced (H = I²Rt) melts it and breaks the circuit.
Why not the others: (A) is used in electric motors and electromagnets. (C) is used in electroplating. (D) is not a basic effect that a fuse uses.
Key point: Fuses are connected in series with the circuit they protect.

questions.sub_topic: Acid in the human stomach
questions.question: Which acid is secreted in the human stomach to help in digestion?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Hydrochloric acid
Why: The stomach lining secretes hydrochloric acid (HCl). It kills germs in food and gives the acidic medium the enzyme pepsin needs.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) are strong industrial acids not made by the body. (D) is found in lemons and oranges.
Key point: Too much acid causes acidity; antacids such as milk of magnesia neutralise it.

questions.sub_topic: Example of ex situ conservation
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of ex situ conservation (conservation outside the natural habitat)?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) A seed bank
Why: A seed bank stores seeds away from where the plants grow naturally, so it is ex situ. Zoos and botanical gardens are other examples.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) protect plants and animals in their natural habitat, which is in situ conservation.
Key point: In situ — in the natural home; ex situ — away from it.

questions.sub_topic: Teacher's age from a change in the average
questions.question: The average age of 30 students is 15 years. When the teacher's age is included, the average rises by 1 year. What is the teacher's age?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 46 years
Given: 30 students, average 15; with the teacher, 31 people, average 16.
Step 1: Students' total = 30 × 15 = 450.
Step 2: Total with teacher = 31 × 16 = 496.
Step 3: Teacher = 496 − 450 = 46 years.
Common mistake: giving the new average (16, option B), or using the shortcut with the old average (15 + 30 × 1 = 45, option D); the shortcut is new average + 30 × 1 = 16 + 30 = 46.

questions.sub_topic: Equal days and nights at the Equator
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Days and nights are of nearly equal length at the Equator throughout the year.
Reason (R): The Earth's axis is tilted at about 23.5° from the perpendicular to the plane of its orbit.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Why: Both are true. The circle of illumination (the line between day and night) always cuts the Equator into two equal halves, so the Equator has about 12 hours of day and night all year. The tilt of the axis explains why day length changes away from the Equator and why seasons occur; it does not explain the equal days at the Equator. So (R) is not the explanation of (A).
Why not the others: (A) wrongly links the two. (C) and (D) call a true statement false.
Key point: Tilt causes the seasons; the Equator is the one place where they do not change day length.

questions.sub_topic: Village with the highest literacy rate
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Population, number of males and number of literate persons in five villages

| Village | Population | Males | Literate persons |
|---|---|---|---|
| Amla | 2000 | 1100 | 1500 |
| Bela | 1600 | 800 | 1200 |
| Chana | 2400 | 1300 | 1440 |
| Dhani | 1200 | 650 | 1020 |
| Elora | 2800 | 1400 | 2240 |

Question: Which village has the highest literacy rate (literate persons as a percentage of the population)?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Dhani
Given: literacy rates — Amla 1500/2000 = 75%; Bela 1200/1600 = 75%; Chana 1440/2400 = 60%; Dhani 1020/1200 = 85%; Elora 2240/2800 = 80%.
Step 1: Compare the rates.
Step 2: The highest is Dhani (85%).
Common mistake: choosing Elora, which has the most literate persons (2240) but a lower rate.

questions.sub_topic: Overall literacy rate of the five villages
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Population, number of males and number of literate persons in five villages

| Village | Population | Males | Literate persons |
|---|---|---|---|
| Amla | 2000 | 1100 | 1500 |
| Bela | 1600 | 800 | 1200 |
| Chana | 2400 | 1300 | 1440 |
| Dhani | 1200 | 650 | 1020 |
| Elora | 2800 | 1400 | 2240 |

Question: What is the literacy rate of the five villages taken together?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 74%
Given: total population = 2000 + 1600 + 2400 + 1200 + 2800 = 10,000; total literate = 1500 + 1200 + 1440 + 1020 + 2240 = 7400.
Step 1: 7400 ÷ 10,000 = 0.74.
Step 2: Literacy rate = 74%.
Common mistake: averaging the five villages' rates ((75 + 75 + 60 + 85 + 80) ÷ 5 = 75%, option B); villages of different sizes must be weighted by their populations.

questions.sub_topic: Ratio of males to females in Chana
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Population, number of males and number of literate persons in five villages

| Village | Population | Males | Literate persons |
|---|---|---|---|
| Amla | 2000 | 1100 | 1500 |
| Bela | 1600 | 800 | 1200 |
| Chana | 2400 | 1300 | 1440 |
| Dhani | 1200 | 650 | 1020 |
| Elora | 2800 | 1400 | 2240 |

Question: What is the ratio of males to females in Chana?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 13 : 11
Given: Chana — population 2400, males 1300.
Step 1: Females = 2400 − 1300 = 1100.
Step 2: Males : females = 1300 : 1100 = 13 : 11.
Common mistake: writing the ratio the other way round (11 : 13, option A), or comparing males with the whole population (1300 : 2400 = 13 : 24, option B).

questions.sub_topic: Total illiterate persons in the five villages
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Population, number of males and number of literate persons in five villages

| Village | Population | Males | Literate persons |
|---|---|---|---|
| Amla | 2000 | 1100 | 1500 |
| Bela | 1600 | 800 | 1200 |
| Chana | 2400 | 1300 | 1440 |
| Dhani | 1200 | 650 | 1020 |
| Elora | 2800 | 1400 | 2240 |

Question: How many persons in the five villages taken together are not literate?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 2600
Given: total population 10,000; total literate 7400.
Step 1: Not literate = 10,000 − 7400 = 2600.
Step 2: (Check by village: 500 + 400 + 960 + 180 + 560 = 2600.)
Common mistake: giving the number of literate persons (7400, option B).

questions.sub_topic: Literate persons in Chana after growth
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Population, number of males and number of literate persons in five villages

| Village | Population | Males | Literate persons |
|---|---|---|---|
| Amla | 2000 | 1100 | 1500 |
| Bela | 1600 | 800 | 1200 |
| Chana | 2400 | 1300 | 1440 |
| Dhani | 1200 | 650 | 1020 |
| Elora | 2800 | 1400 | 2240 |

Question: Next year, the population of Chana is expected to rise by 25% and its literacy rate to rise to 70%. How many literate persons will Chana then have?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 2100
Given: Chana's population now 2400; literacy rate next year 70%.
Step 1: New population = 2400 × 1.25 = 3000.
Step 2: Literate persons = 70% of 3000 = 2100.
Common mistake: keeping the old literacy rate of 60% (1800, option B), or applying 70% to the old population (1680, option D).
